xxx:
In a normal organization the workday starts noticeably earlier than any of the workers might be needed. Say if the store opens at 8, the staff arrives at 7:30. So being up to 15 minutes late doesn't affect anything at all. Regular latecomers get fined so it doesn't become a system, nobody cares about the rest.
A normal organization has staff redundancy accounting for vacations, holidays and sick leaves (on average 10 weeks out of 52 a person doesn't work, i.e. the staff needs to be increased by 25%, right now we have a department of 4 shift workers and their boss, so the department head goes out with a subordinate for a month or two a year, the rest of the time he covers someone at the post).
Staff redundancy also determines interchangeability. If someone stepped out to eat, smoke or use the toilet — it doesn't affect production. But if someone is constantly stepped out — the team won't love them.
Of course everywhere there are strange individuals who don't work at all. But they're the ones who come to work 30 minutes early so nobody notices them any extra. And ask the general director personally if they need to leave. And don't go out to smoke.
